name: Dokshi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Shimizu 1978 South Bauchi survey (wordlist) and Decker & Araokanmi 2022 sociolinguistic profile of the Zeem cluster; no grammar or phonology of Dokshi exists in Glottolog's 8 references.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken & Thelma Araokanmi. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Zeem Cluster [zua] Languages of Bauchi and Plateau State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-013. SIL International. viii+56 pp. (downloaded from Internet Archive copy of sil.org)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 8.3 'Phonetic inventory' (pp. 22-24) gives cluster-wide consonant and vowel charts including the Dokshi (Lukshi village, Dass LGA) 222-item wordlist, and 8.5 discusses segmental correspondences; Appendix F (p. 44) states 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the report.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2022. Change Request 2022-030 (split of [zua]; creation of [dsk] Dokshi etc.). SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; notes Dokshi, Tulai and Zeem 'are no longer actively spoken' and gives lexical-similarity percentages from Decker & Araokanmi 2022.

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2011. Number in South-Bauchi West languages (Chadic, Nigeria). Paper presented at 'Number in Africa and Beyond', Cologne, Sept. 2011. HAL halshs-00645133, 16 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Dokshi data at all; fn. 1 (p. 2): 'Luri, Zeem, Tule and Lushi are now extinct.'

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2006. South-Bauchi West Pronominal and TAM Systems. In Caron & Zima (eds.), Sprachbund in the West African Sahel, 93-112. Peeters. (and 2003 CIL17 preprint version)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Dokshi; lists Shimizu's language no. 21 'Dokshi (Lushi)' in the Zeem subgroup and states 'Caari is the only surviving language of the Zeem subgroup, the other three (Zeem, Tule and Dokshi) being extinct'.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2005. The Dyarim language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment, Cambridge, 22 Nov 2005.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Dokshi prosody; states of the Zeem cluster (Zeem, Danshe, Lushi) 'The main, and indeed only, source on these languages is Shimizu (1978)'; cites a few Dokshi cognate forms in wordlist comments.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page lush1256 'Dokshi' (alt. Lukshi, Lushi); AES 'Extinct', Ethnologue EGIDS 9 (Dormant).
sources.note: Nothing; only refs are Shimizu 1978 and Decker & Araokanmi 2022; zero grammar/phonology/sketch references.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken et al. (forthcoming 2022d). A sociolinguistic profile of some endangered West Chadic B.3 languages in South Bauchi State, Nigeria with notes on Dulubu [dbo]. Journal of Language Survey Reports. SIL International.

sources.note: Companion SIL survey of neighbouring South Bauchi B.3 (Dass-area) varieties; if Dokshi is treated with the Dass cluster it may carry further Lukshi data, though SIL surveys do not normally analyse stress.

sources.citation: SIL Nigeria survey field recordings and full 222-item Dokshi (Lukshi) wordlist audio, 2021 (underlying Decker & Araokanmi 2022 Appendix F/G).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only known recorded Dokshi speech from the last rememberers; any future stress statement would have to be derived from these recordings.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. The South Bauchi languages of Central Nigeria: a fresh view based on recent fieldwork. Powerpoint presented at CALL 50, Leiden University, 31 August 2020.

sources.note: Cited by Decker & Araokanmi as recent South Bauchi fieldwork overview; could contain new Dokshi/Lukshi data or classification notes (Blench 2020a alternately places Dokshi in the Dass cluster).
